IN THE INTEREST  OF JUSTICE.
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:18125  CRL.P No. 103116 of 2024  THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MOHAMMAD NAWAZ  ORAL ORDER

This is a successive bail petition filed by accused No.1 praying to enlarge him on bail in a case pending in S.C.No.31/2023 on the file of the Court of Principal District and Sessions Judge, Gadag,
arising out of Crime No.181/2022 of Nargund Police Station, Gadag.

entities.text: Court of Principal District and Sessions Judge, Gadag
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard both sides and perused the material on record.
3.

Charge sheet is filed against accused Nos.1 to 4 for offences punishable under Section 304B,
498A, 302, 201, 114 r/w 34 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of the DP Act.
4. The complaint is lodged by victim's mother alleging that her daughter Deepa @ Nandini was given in marriage to the petitioner/accused No.1 about 2  years prior to the date of incident.
Her husband and her in-laws NC: 2024:KHC-D:18125 were demanding her daughter to bring money and gold.
In this connection, they were giving physical and mental torture to her.
About 4 to 5 months prior, they had assaulted her and a month prior, her daughter had requested the complainant to take her back to her parental home and therefore, she was brought to their house.
Since her husband i.e., the petitioner had threatened that he will give divorce, about ten days prior to the date of incident, she was sent back to her matrimonial home.

On 04.12.2022 at about 12.30 p.m.,
complainant was informed that her daughter has committed suicide by hanging.

5. On completion of investigation, Police have filed charge sheet alleging that on 04.12.2022 at about 10.00 a.m., the accused have committed the murder of complainant's daughter Smt. Deepa @
Nandini.

According to the prosecution, accused Nos.2 and 3 have held the hands of the deceased,
accused No.4 instigated and NC: 2024:KHC-D:18125 accused No.1 compressed the face and neck of the deceased with a saree and committed her murder.
6.

The learned counsel for petitioner would contend that accused Nos.2 to 4 are enlarged on bail by this Court and the petitioner is innocent and he has not committed any offence as alleged by the Vinod S/O Yallappa Vaddar vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94021340/
2 prosecution.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He contended that the entire case rests on circumstantial evidence and the say of the prosecution that the petitioner has committed the murder is without any material and the witnesses namely CWs.19 and 20 have not witnessed the petitioner committing the offence.
It is submitted that the petitioner is languishing in judicial custody since 05.12.2022 and therefore, sought to allow the petition and enlarge the petitioner on bail by imposing any conditions.
7. Prayer is opposed by the learned High Court Government Pleader.
He contended that the offence committed by the petitioner is heinous in nature.
In the event of grant of bail to the petitioner, he may threaten NC: 2024:KHC-D:18125 the prosecution witnesses and thereby hamper the case of prosecution.

8. The prayer of the petitioner for bail was rejected by this Court in Crl.P.No.102538/2023 vide order dated 23.11.2023, noticing the Post Mortem report, wherein light finger marks were present and also considering that the main allegations are against the petitioner/accused No.1 that he throttled the deceased.
The material on record shows that the petitioner was subjecting the deceased to physical and mental cruelty demanding her to get money from her parental home.
Accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents and accused No.4 is the Sister of accused No.1.
Grant of bail to the said accused is not a ground to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
9. Considering the nature of offence, period of incarceration undergone by the petitioner is also not a ground to grant bail to the petitioner at this stage.

However, considering that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 05.12.2022, liberty is reserved to him to file NC: 2024:KHC-D:18125 a fresh petition before the Sessions Court, if the trial is not commenced within a period of 4 months.
Petition is accordingly dismissed.
